title: User Story
description: Durable CONTEXT for a feature — why it exists, in the user's terms. Not a work ticket: a story is never 'done', only current, stale, or retired. Delivery lives in wi_* work items outside this database. Source: supabase/migrations/004_story_and_acceptance_criterion.sql

key.description: Globally unique (not per product). The pattern IS a database CHECK: key::text ~ '^story_[a-z0-9]{6}$'. Stored as citext, so uniqueness is case-insensitive, but the CHECK itself is case-sensitive — uppercase is rejected.

status.description: story_status enum. 'stale' is AUTHOR-DECLARED and is distinct from derived low confidence, which the story_confidence view computes from last_reviewed_at age. A story can be one without being the other.

last_reviewed_at.description: Nullable. Feeds the story_confidence view's decay; null means never reviewed.

importance.description: Relative weight of this story against its siblings. A story that no longer reflects our users is TUNED DOWN rather than retired, which is why this is a number and not a status. Orthogonal to `status`: 'stale' questions whether the description is still accurate, importance weights how much we'd care if it were. Consumers rank by it when more stories exist than fit in context. Source: supabase/migrations/018_planning_fields.sql

$comment: PARENTAGE NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: a story attaches to exactly one feature via feature_has_story, which carries UNIQUE (story_id). There is no ac_has_story table — stories and acceptance criteria are siblings under a feature, deliberately not parent and child.
